why: The border IS the shape here, not a boundary around one. A spinner is a ring drawn as a 2px border at 25% of currentColor with one edge (border-t-current) fully opaque, rotated by the motion layer; the arc that reads as progress is the difference between those two edges. There is no fill and no inset shadow that draws a partial ring, and a step in paper tone cannot rotate. RULES.md 2.7 rules on strokes that SEPARATE two things, which this does not.

The same spinner arc, inlined into the button's own busy state rather than imported, so that a busy button never depends on Spinner's own layout. Identical shape, identical reason, and the two are checked together: if one stops drawing its ring the rot check deletes that entry and leaves this one, which is the signal that they have drifted apart.

A drop target, and RULES.md 2.7's own sentence blesses it: form fields and selection controls are the two places a hairline is allowed at all. The dashed edge is also doing work no fill can do — dashed is the one stroke style that reads as PROVISIONAL, which is what an empty drop zone is saying, and the same element restates it in the destructive tone when a file is rejected.

Not a colour: `0 0 #0000` is CSS's way of writing a shadow that paints nothing, set on --hairline-strong to switch OFF the note field's ring for the one composer that must not look like a field. `transparent` would be a named colour, which RULES.md 2.2 refuses outright, so the four-digit hex is the least-wrong spelling of nothing available. If tokens.css ever declares a --shadow-none, this line goes with it.
